story: Tim Perry formed the Portland collective in 2008, and Willamette Week named it Portland's best new band of 2011; the name became Ages and Ages in 2013. Divisionary came out on Partisan on March 25, 2014, produced by Tony Lash, and Paste called it full of goosebump-raising hooks. They played Pickathon in 2011 and returned that summer. Something to Ruin followed in 2016 and Me You They We in 2019, and Fine Thanks and You in March 2026, with Perry still leading.

intro: A Dallas soul singer, songwriter and DJ.
story: Bobby Patterson was born on March 13, 1944, in Dallas, and wrote and recorded Dallas soul in the 1960s and '70s, including "T.C.B. or T.Y.A." Golden Smog later recorded "She Don't Have to See You," which he co-wrote, and he hosted a KKDA soul radio show from 1997 to 2012. A SXSW performance in March 2014 led to I Got More Soul!, recorded in Austin and released on Omnivore on July 22; the Austin Chronicle called it the comeback Patterson deserves, and he played Pickathon that summer.
artist_reel_line: I Got More Soul! came out on Omnivore on July 22, 2014.

story: Charlie Parr is a folk-blues singer from Duluth, Minnesota, who began recording in 2002 with Criminals & Sinners and plays resonator guitar and open-back banjo. Barnswallow, his eleventh studio album, came out in February 2013, engineered by Tom Herbers. He played Pickathon in 2011 and again in 2014. He signed with Red House Records in 2015 and released Stumpjumper, produced with Phil Cook, and Dog in 2017; Sing Out! named Stumpjumper a best of 2015.
artist_reel_line: Stumpjumper, with Phil Cook, came out on Red House in 2015.

intro: A North Carolina duo, here for the first of five visits.
story: Andrew Marlin and Emily Frantz, a married couple, began playing together in 2009 in Chapel Hill. This Side of Jordan came out on August 19, 2013, their first for Yep Roc after self-released albums, and NPR named it one of its top ten folk and Americana albums. They first played Pickathon in 2014 and returned in 2015, 2017, 2019 and 2023. In April 2021 they changed their name to Watchhouse, Marlin saying the old name was born out of his 21-year-old mind, and Rituals came out on Thirty Tigers in 2025.

Operators is the synth-rock band of Dan Boeckner of Wolf Parade, Handsome Furs and Divine Fits, with the keyboardist Devojka and the Divine Fits drummer Sam Brown. EP1 came out on Last Gang in 2014, the year they played Pickathon. Blue Wave, their first album, produced by Graham Walsh, came out on Last Gang on April 1, 2016, and Radiant Dawn in May 2019, which Stereogum made its Album of the Week.

intro: An underground hip-hop duo of crate-dug beats.
story: Thes One, Chris Portugal, and Double K, Michael Turner, formed People Under the Stairs in Los Angeles in 1997, sharing rapping, DJing and producing. Highlighter, their eighth album, came out on September 30, 2011, the first on Thes One's own Piecelock 70 label, and 12 Step Program followed in 2014, the year they played Pickathon. They wrapped up with Sincerely, The P on February 1, 2019, and Double K died in 2021. Thes One has gone on producing, lecturing and releasing archival material, among it Project 1992.

intro: A Portland soul veteran with a late-career revival.
story: Ural Thomas was born on December 21, 1939, in Louisiana, and began recording in the 1960s, stepped away from the industry for decades, then teamed with the drummer and DJ Scott Magee to form the Pain in the early 2010s. The Portland Mercury called him a deep soul hero who hasn't hit the national consciousness the way Charles Bradley has. They played Pickathon in 2014. Ural Thomas & the Pain came out on Mississippi Records in 2016 and The Right Time in 2018, and Dancing Dimensions on Bella Union on June 3, 2022, which Hot Press called a near-perfect summer record.
artist_reel_line: Dancing Dimensions came out on Bella Union on June 3, 2022.

intro: A Los Angeles art-rock quartet of hypnotic interplay.
story: Warpaint formed in Los Angeles in 2004: Emily Kokal, Theresa Wayman, Jenny Lee Lindberg and, later, the drummer Stella Mozgawa. Their self-titled second album came out on Rough Trade on January 17, 2014, four years after The Fool, produced by Flood and the band, and NPR's First Listen said it feels fashionable but never at the expense of approachability. The Skinny made it its number one album of 2014, and they played Pickathon that summer. Heads Up followed in 2016 and Radiate Like This in 2022.

intro: Los Angeles punk pioneers, by then elder statesmen.
story: John Doe and Billy Zoom founded X in Los Angeles in 1977, finding each other through want ads; Doe's partner Exene Cervenka became co-lead singer, with the drummer D.J. Bonebrake. Los Angeles, from 1980, and Wild Gift, from 1981, were both produced by the Doors' Ray Manzarek, and both land among Rolling Stone's 500 greatest albums. They played Pickathon in 2014 and received the Icon Award at the 2015 Alternative Press Music Awards. Alphabetland came in 2020 and Smoke & Fiction, billed as their final studio album, in 2024.
